subject: SLA template negotiation — anchored uptime and capped monthly remedy
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@evergreen.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@evergreen.ai>
Date: 2025-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Procurement SLA template — request to align uptime/remedy

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we had a couple follow-ups from procurement. Attached is our standard procurement SLA template. The two asks that matter heavily for legal are:

- Anchor uptime at a fixed percent (we usually request 99.99% for customer-facing APIs).
- Prefer a fixed monthly remedy (simple credit cap) rather than a sliding percentage tied only to downtime buckets.

Can Redwood agree to an anchored uptime point and a capped monthly remedy ($ or % of invoice)? If not, please propose a compromise we can run by our counsel.

For context: Evergreen needs predictability for forecasting and prefers a single monthly credit cap rather than variable monthly percentages. We can be flexible on maintenance carve-outs if you can clearly matrix them.

Attachment: Evergreen_Procurement_Template.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Procurement — Evergreen AI
elena.ruiz@evergreen.ai
+1 415-555-0192
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@evergreen.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement SLA template — request to align uptime/remedy

Hi Elena — really appreciate the note and the template. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (rev ops) so we can respond with a pragmatic amendment.

Short answer: we can anchor availability and provide a capped monthly remedy, but the specific percentages and cap levels depend on the deployment footprint (hosted vs. dedicated) and whether you need additional latency SLAs for critical endpoints. Proposed starting points below:

- Hosted API availability anchor: 99.95% monthly uptime.
- Optional elevated anchor: 99.99% for a narrowly defined set of "control" or critical endpoints (admin, billing, webhook delivery) — would require additional monitoring hooks.
- Remedy: capped monthly credit equal to 10% of that month’s Redwood invoice for the service (flat cap).
- Maintenance carve-out: scheduled maintenance (with 72-hour notice) carved out up to 6 hours/month; emergency maintenance limited but we provide post-incident notes.

If Evergreen prefers a simple $ cap instead of %, we can convert the cap using your projected monthly committed spend.

I've attached a draft SLA amendment (Redwood_SLA_Amendment_Draft_v1.pdf) with the anchor and cap framed as above. If Laura/legal have redlines, happy to iterate rapidly.

Next steps: if that structure looks reasonable, can we schedule a 30-min sync today or tomorrow to align on which endpoints (if any) need the elevated 99.99% anchor and confirm the cap approach?

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Amendment_Draft_v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
(415) 555-0128
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@evergreen.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@evergreen.ai>
Date: 2025-08-30T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement SLA template — request to align uptime/remedy

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the quick reply and the draft. A few clarifications from our counsel and ops:

- Evergreen is open to 99.95% as a baseline for general API traffic, but our customer-facing inference endpoints carry higher risk for us. We will push for 99.99% on those endpoints.
- We understand the monitoring requirement — if Redwood can provide per-endpoint p95 and p99 latency reporting and incident traces for the elevated endpoints, that will help justify the elevated anchor.
- Regarding the remedy cap: a 10% cap tied to the invoice is a reasonable starting point. Procurement would prefer a $25k monthly cap for the first year (whichever is lower: 10% or $25k) — that gives Evergreen a clear budgeting ceiling.

I've attached a redline summary from our counsel (short notes in the PDF). I can do a call tomorrow morning PT to walk through.

Attachment: Evergreen_Redlines_Summary.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Elena
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@evergreen.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-31T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement SLA template — request to align uptime/remedy

Elena — thanks for the redlines and the call offer. 

Quick reply and proposed compromise (so legal and ops have a concrete position):

- Baseline: Hosted API anchor at 99.95% monthly uptime.
- Elevated: We will designate up to three customer-specified endpoints as "elevated" for 99.99% uptime; Redwood will expose p95/p99 latency dashboards and a webhook-based incident feed for those endpoints. 
- Remedy cap: Monthly credit capped at the lesser of 10% of monthly Redwood charges or $25,000 for the first 12 months. After year 1, we can revisit the cap against committed volume.
- Maintenance carve-outs: Scheduled maintenance (<= 6 hours/month) with 72-hour notice will be excluded; emergency maintenance will be rare and remediated per our incident SLA.

Marissa (CS) — can you confirm operational feasibility for supporting up to three elevated endpoints with the monitoring hooks? We want to make sure we can meet the 99.99% target if Evergreen marks those endpoints.

If this compromise looks acceptable to Evergreen, I can convert the draft to a DocuSign-ready amendment and loop in Laura to sign off on tightened legal language. For tracking, I've also uploaded a short monthly remedy workbook (Monthly_Remedy_Worksheet.xlsx) to the deal in HubSpot.
